interactions.title: Opening reports: Alesh and the Shakun initiates
lines: DM: To the south, Alesh and her small group of companions ride quickly through the deserts, hopefully avoiding danger and seeking to learn what lurks in the ruins of Bas Udda and other points beyond, and return to Karawa with knowledge to prepare for what may come. In Karawa, the fate of the acolytes and initiates of the Shakun mysteries, holed up in the temple of Shakun, is unknown. Centaurs now ride fast towards these defenders, bringing the warning of a spreading plague and perhaps aid in battle as well, if it is not too late already.

before: DM: In the West, a tired mass of refugees fled Karawa nine days ago.
Wellby: [garbled]
DM: Out. Yes.
Unknown: Great idea.

DM: Nine days ago, while you were waiting for the festival to begin—rumors of attacks, this—yep, here we go. Rumors of attacks, rampaging creatures half human, half hyena and full of violence, reach Karawa, which was later attacked by these gnolls and worse, a few days later. Now, some nine days later, the refugees should hopefully be nearing the river Hara on the outskirts of Tokra if no danger has overwhelmed them on the way.
after: DM: To the east, few dare to tread. The ancient wards protecting the borders of Dunmar have fallen, and the dangers that were held at bay have emerged again.
DM: In the north, everything is unnaturally still and quiet. Nothing moves on the lands where the mountains meet the plains.
DM: In the mountain valley and holdfast of Raven's Hold, some force of evil out of the diseased hell of the Abyss lurks.
DM: Beneath the mountains, you all breathe a sigh of relief, having moments ago defeated a roper, a many-tentacled stalagmite creature with a vicious bite.

DM: Now, looking around the mangled remains of this beast, crashed against the floor of this huge dwarven marketplace, strong acid running out of its wounds with a few bits of partially digested bone, whatever else may remain of its previous victims.

interactions.title: Seeker attunes to the Pearl of Power
lines: Seeker: Can I try it, then?
Seeker: Pearl of Power, okay, and add it.

DM: And Seeker, as you're resting, you—it, it almost feels like—it does feel like a spring uncoiling, like as you're sort of focusing on this this pearl. This—this energy kind of is released almost all of a sudden, and you feel the power restoring to you. And then as you're kind of contemplating it, as you're attuning to it, you can feel it kind of slowly drawing in energy from the—from the land around you. Just kind of pulling on whatever ley lines or energy. ((Hit Dice mechanics))
DM: ((Rest mechanics)) You can feel it sort of slowly kind of gathering in this energy, and you figure over time it will accumulate enough more energy to then be released all at once.

interactions.title: Kenzo describes a tentacled leader in a borrowed memory
lines: Kenzo: Before we go further, Riswynn, you—I, I had a strange, strange, strange almost vision or memory when we first entered this cavern of a—small creatures, but that they were, they were led by something. They were led by a, by a creature. Tall, tall. Tall, human, human-like creature with tentacles from its mouth. You know such creatures living here?

Riswynn: I mean, that could fall in the category of monsters that one comes across when one is on these sorts of adventures, but otherwise never heard of except in childhood stories. Not like, ‘Oh yeah, that's what killed my mom.’
Seeker: Kenzo, you said that—[garbled] Good. Good to hear. These, these dwarf-like creatures, you're saying they triggered the vision? And you—when did you see this thing that you're saying? So—

Kenzo: Early, earlier. Earlier in the cavern I had a memory that wasn't mine, but I—I worried that these—I don't know if it's this cavern or another cavern, but there's—they're connected somehow, these, these creatures and this, um, Tim, would we call it mind flayers? Is that like a common thing, like we would actually know what they are?
DM: Yeah, I mean, you'd have heard legends and rumors of those. Yeah.

Kenzo: Yeah. Yeah. But I think, I think these have some relation to mind flayers, these, these creatures. And she spoke about earlier. Just now, didn't she, didn't she not? She said something about something that would—
Kenzo: That would eat our brains. Yes.
Seeker: Kenzo, does, it does that suggest to you that one such creature's living down in the vault?

Kenzo: I don't know, I don't know. I, I just know that they're related. I know that these creatures are somehow related to mind flayers, and based on what our friend just said, um, you should just be very careful where—as we, as we head, as we head farther down. Wellby: I'll say, ‘Ah, look. Whoever you are, wherever you are, it's—we should just talk now. We don't want to go through this whole process. We don't want to like find you and track you, like let's just have the conversation.’

And then where the entryway is, there's sort of, there's like a few spots that are worn along the side, like where maybe a hinge was attached. review.reason: The voice and surrounding dialogue strongly suggest Inakara, but the DM’s explicit identification remains unfinished.

interactions.title: The two hidden keys open the vault
lines: Seeker: I'm look—I'm looking from the door to one of the statues and back repeatedly. It looks like—that's weird. The reflection of one of the statues has a, has a necklace on, but the statue doesn't have a necklace on, if you know what I mean. And it's just one of the two?
Wellby: What does the necklace look like?
Seeker: A little—probably a little hard to investigate. I get my face up close to the mirror.
DM: Yeah, it's like having a hard time getting a clear look at it. You just are sort of noticing something hanging, nothing that clicks in your mind about what it is, but—
Seeker: Oh, only in the center door, I was asking.
DM: Are you going to go look at a different door?
Seeker: I'll try the right-hand door.

Seeker: Hmm. OK, so now that I'm at the right-hand door, I'm going to like try to keep the line of sight between the two—the statue and the surface—and like step back and try to reach up to where the necklace is on the statue.
DM: ((Crossing the low wall)) There's definitely something dangling on its neck.
Seeker: So I can feel it in my hand?
Delwath: So does this only show up in the door? Are we looking in an actual like a mirror?
DM: You don't see anything anywhere on the statues.
Delwath: What do you—what is Seeker looking through? It just at the door?
Seeker: The door is like reflective. Yeah.
Riswynn: Do I see this as I look in the reflection of the doors? Right. Delwath, he looks in the reflection of the doors.
DM: Are you looking in there? Yeah, the doors? Nope.
Kenzo: I look into the reflection of the doors.
DM: Nothing but just the room.
Seeker: And meanwhile, I'm sort of feeling around this necklace with my fingertips.
DM: That's right. It's just like a key.
Seeker: That's interesting. It feels like a key. But there's no visible keyhole, is there? No. ((Hypothetical trap joke))
Riswynn: Try this on the other side.

DM: Yeah, the same thing. You—you're now, after having watched Seeker almost tripped over the wall, you're well aware of it and carefully, like, negotiate—navigate around the wall while still keeping your eye at the door, and you also feel a key around the other statue.

DM: Okay, as you lift these necklaces off the statues, um, Riswynn, you see a small hole open in the door directly in front of you on the left side of the room. And Seeker, you see the same thing on the right side of the room. The middle door does not change.
